headline: Delhi HC: Vacancy allowance u/s 23(1)(c) available for units let earlier but vacant in year
reference: PCIT-3 vs DLF Ltd., ITA 126/2019, Delhi High Court, decided 18 November 2026 (AY 2007-08)
summary_points: Issue: whether notional rent (ALV) of ₹3,28,52,595 on 4 vacant commercial units could be taxed under Sections 22 and 23 for AY 2007-08.
Held: Section 23(1)(c) applies where property was let in earlier years and stayed vacant despite genuine efforts to re-let; ALV is then nil.
The Court agreed with the Andhra Pradesh High Court's Vivek Jain view and distinguished Ansal Housing, where the units were never let out.
Questions 1 to 4 were treated as covered by earlier Delhi HC rulings; the Revenue's appeal was dismissed as raising no substantial question of law.
who_is_affected: Real estate developers and property owners with vacant let-out or unsold properties, and Revenue officers assessing notional rent under house property income.
action_required: Maintain documentary proof of earlier letting and ongoing efforts to re-let vacant units to support a vacancy claim under Section 23(1)(c).

Delhi High Court on notional rent for vacant property: PCIT-3 vs DLF Ltd. (ITA 126/2019, decided 18 November 2026).

The Revenue challenged the deletion of an addition of ₹3,28,52,595 as notional rent (ALV) on vacant units for AY 2007-08.

The Court held that Section 23(1)(c) gives relief where a property was let in earlier years and remained vacant in the relevant year despite genuine efforts to find a tenant. In such cases, the ALV is nil.

The Court distinguished Ansal Housing & Constructions, where the properties had never been let out, and agreed with the Andhra Pradesh High Court's view in Vivek Jain.

The Revenue's appeal was dismissed, as no substantial question of law arose.

Practical takeaway: keep evidence of past tenancies and efforts to re-let, such as affidavits and records, when claiming vacancy relief.
